# Saturation mutagenesis: DeepLoc + protGPS on every RBP point mutant

Full missense saturation scan (every residue -> all 19 other amino
acids) across the 2,336 RBPs in `../rbp_filter/rbp_wt_list_with_go.tsv`,
scored for subcellular localization (DeepLoc2.1) and condensate
partitioning (protGPS).

## Data source -- not regenerated by this repo

The mutant sequences themselves come from a labmate's (asharma)
independently-built file:

```
/u/project/kappel/asharma/RBP/saturation_mutagenesis/rbp_satmut_all.csv.gz
```

33,184,720 rows: 1,659,236 `is_wt=True` reference rows (one per residue
across all proteins) + 31,525,484 actual mutant rows (19 x 1,659,236,
confirming it's a complete per-residue scan). Columns include
`uniprot_accession, RBP_name, position, wt_aa, mut_aa, mutation, is_wt,
sequence` plus several MANE-transcript-mapping columns.

**This repo does not generate that file and has no copy of asharma's
own generation code.** Reproducing this specific step requires either
that exact file (checksum it if you copy it elsewhere) or asharma's
original script. Everything below starts from that file as a given
input.

## Pipeline

1. **`build_chunks_from_satmut_source.py`** -- streams the gzipped CSV,
   skips `is_wt=True` rows, writes FASTA chunks (header
   `>{uniprot_accession}|{RBP_name}|{mutation}`) of 140,000 sequences
   each to `satmut_chunks/chunk_NNNN.fasta`, plus a
   `satmut_manifest.tsv` (per-protein mutant counts). Produced 226
   chunks, 31,525,484 sequences written -- matches the source exactly.

2. **`submit_satmut_deeploc_array.sh`** -- DeepLoc2.1 array job, one
   task per chunk, 226 tasks. Each task writes to
   `satmut_deeploc_results/chunk_NNNN/` and ends with a hard
   correctness check (`exit 1` unless output row count >= input count),
   so a truncated/killed task shows up as a real job failure, not a
   half-written file that looks done.

3. **`submit_satmut_protgps_array.sh`** -- protGPS array job, same
   chunking, pinned to the lab's dedicated `kappel_gpu.q` node only.
   Same correctness-check pattern. protGPS is far cheaper per chunk
   (~27-32 min vs. DeepLoc's ~5.5-7h) so it isn't subject to the
   GPU-scheduling issues below.

4. **`submit_satmut_deeploc_retry.sh`** -- backfill script for chunks
   that failed outright (see below). Edit the `CHUNKS=(...)` array and
   the `#$ -t 1-N` count to match, then `qsub` it.

## GPU scheduling: the account-wide cap and the queue-list fix

Submitting `submit_satmut_deeploc_array.sh` with no `-q` restriction
(the very first version) stalled at 2 concurrent tasks no matter what
`-tc` was set to. `qconf -srqs gpu` showed why: a hard per-account
resource-quota rule caps this account at **4 concurrent GPUs across the
entire general shared pool**, summed over every `gpu_*.q` queue
together -- not a per-queue or per-job limit.

Restricting the job to only the fast queues
(`-q gpu_l40s.q,gpu_a100.q,gpu_h100.q`) to try to speed up individual
chunks was a mistake: it dropped concurrency further (to 1), since none
of those queues had a free slot and the job could no longer fall back
to the slower `gpu_RTX2080Ti.q` it had been using. The fix that actually
works is SGE's **hard/soft queue split**, used in the two array scripts
above:

```
#$ -q gpu_RTX2080Ti.q,gpu_l40s.q,gpu_a100.q,gpu_h100.q   # hard: anywhere in this set
#$ -soft -q gpu_l40s.q,gpu_a100.q,gpu_h100.q              # soft: prefer these if free
```

This lets the scheduler grab a fast GPU when one's open, but never
blocks waiting for one -- it falls back to RTX2080Ti (which reliably
finishes a 140k-sequence chunk in ~5.5-7.2h) rather than sitting idle.

### Why the hard list excludes `gpu_smp.q` / `gpu_rh7.q`

An earlier attempt loosened the hard list to `*` (any queue on the
cluster) to maximize fallback options. Two tasks landed on
`gpu_smp.q`/`gpu_rh7.q` -- large, general-purpose, heavily shared
queues -- and both ran the full 8-hour `h_rt` wall-time limit without
finishing, then got SIGKILLed (`qacct` shows `failed=44` / "execd
enforced h_rt limit", `exit_status=137`). `qhost -F cuda` on those
nodes showed `hc:cuda=0` (no free GPU capacity) at dispatch time --
they're not dedicated GPU nodes, and heavy contention from unrelated
jobs made them far slower than RTX2080Ti for this workload. SGE does
**not** auto-retry a task killed this way; the chunk is just silently
dropped from the run unless you notice and backfill it yourself.

Net effect across the run so far: tasks landed on these two queues five
times before the hard list was narrowed back down to the four
known-good queues above. All five (chunks 5, 6, 9, 10, 11) had to be
resubmitted via `submit_satmut_deeploc_retry.sh`.

**Lesson:** when widening a hard queue list for fallback purposes,
widen it to specific named queues you've checked have real dedicated
GPU capacity (`qhost -h <host> -F cuda`, looking for consistent
non-zero `hc:cuda` capacity, not just a momentary free count) --
not to `*`.

### Verifying completion -- always by content, never by queue state alone

`qstat` showing a task as finished (or not in the queue) doesn't mean
it succeeded -- see the silent-failure case above. Verify every chunk
by comparing real row counts:

```bash
D=/u/project/kappel/ddcohn/protein_variant_effects/rbp_only
for c in $(ls $D/satmut_deeploc_results); do
  n_in=$(grep -c '^>' $D/satmut_chunks/${c}.fasta)
  f=$(ls $D/satmut_deeploc_results/$c/results_*.csv 2>/dev/null | head -1)
  n_out=$([ -n "$f" ] && echo $(($(wc -l < "$f") - 1)) || echo MISSING)
  [ "$n_out" != "$n_in" ] && echo "MISMATCH: $c in=$n_in out=$n_out"
done
```

And cross-check exit status directly against the scheduler's own
record rather than trusting a script's log output, since a process
killed by `h_rt` never reaches its own completion `echo`:

```bash
qacct -j <job_id> -t <task_id> | grep -E 'qname|failed|exit_status|ru_wallclock'
```

## Sharing a "dedicated" node with the general pool

`kappel_gpu.q` runs on a specific physical host that also has a general
-pool queue definition (`gpu_l40s.q`) on the same hardware. The lab's
RQS exemption gives this account rights to both GPUs on that box, but
if an unrelated user's job lands there first via the general queue,
only one GPU is actually free for us even though the node is nominally
"ours." Not a bug, not a permissions change -- just two queue
definitions sharing one host. Check `qhost -h <host> -F cuda` for the
real free count rather than assuming the dedicated queue's capacity is
exclusively available.
